# I/O cheatsheet

The whole of entity I/O on one screen. The long version is [[io-concepts]].

### 1. Output fires
The entity emits a signal, like `pressed(activator)`.

### 2. Times, then delay
The fire is counted against *Times*, then waits *Delay* seconds.

### 3. Resolve target
The target selector becomes a list of nodes. None found means nothing happens.

### 4. Call input
The input method is called on each node with the parameter.

## Targets

| Write | Reaches |
| --- | --- |
| `main_door` | That targetname, in the same map |
| `door_*` | Targetnames starting with `door_` |
| `@enemies` | The Godot group, whole tree |
| `!player` | First node in group `player` |
| `!activator` | Who started the chain (`!caller` too) |
| `!self` | The entity with the output |
| `/root/Game` | An absolute node path |

## Parameters

A plain value is tried as int, float, bool, then `x y z` as a `Vector3`, else it stays a string. `[a, b]` in JSON spreads into several arguments.

Placeholders `$activator`, `$self`, `$position` and `$caller_name` are filled in on the **receiving** entity.

No parameter: the activator goes into the first object argument.

## Who keeps the activator

**Pass it on** `triggered`, `pressed`, `entered`, `exited`, `hurt`, `teleported`, `pushed`
**Replace it** `arrived(corner)`, `spawned(node)`, `reached(train)`
**Drop it** `opened`, `timer`, `step_N`, `on_true`, `broken`, `switched`, `map_spawn`

Lost it? Target `!player` instead.

## Inputs any node has

`kill`, `show`, `hide`, `enable`, `disable`, `toggle`, used when no method of that name exists. An unknown input with a parameter sets the property of that name instead.

## logic_script scope

`this`, `activator`, `parameter`, `io` and `tree`. Indent with tabs.

## Nothing happened?

> [!TIP] Check in this order
> The Issues panel for unknown targetnames, the Logic panel to fire the chain, F3 in game for what actually fired, and `GodotTrenchIO.events()` to log every output.
